question: What is the primary goal of a research critique in nursing?

options.A: To summarize the background of a study
options.B: To rewrite the methodology section completely
options.C: To judge scientific merit and clinical relevance
options.D: To rewrite the author's original hypothesis

explanation: A critique evaluates the overall quality and usefulness of a study rather than just summarizing it. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h1)

question: How does a critique differ from a simple research summary?

options.A: A critique only looks at the abstract and references
options.B: A summary includes statistical analysis of the raw data
options.C: A critique assesses the strengths and weaknesses of the study
options.D: A summary provides a deep judgment of ethical violations

explanation: While a summary merely restates what the authors did, a critique actively evaluates how well they did it. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why must nurses evaluate research before changing hospital ward procedures?

options.A: Not all published studies use sound scientific methods
options.B: Patients always demand the newest medications available
options.C: Older nursing textbooks are completely useless for practice
options.D: Hospital management requires two journal reviews per month

explanation: Publication does not guarantee flawless execution, so nurses must screen out methodologically weak studies. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: A staff nurse wants to change wound care based on one journal article. What is the best next step?

options.A: Ask the hospital accountant to buy the described supplies
options.B: Hide the article so doctors do not read it first
options.C: Critique the article to check its validity and safety
options.D: Immediately apply the new method to all surgical patients

explanation: Direct adoption of unverified research findings can compromise patient safety. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is an essential ethical check during a research critique?

options.A: Checking the personal income of the lead author
options.B: Ensuring the study was funded by a government body
options.C: Confirming the paper has at least fifty pages
options.D: Verification of informed consent and ethical approval

explanation: Ethical integrity regarding human subjects is non-negotiable in any credible nursing research. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why should a nurse maintain objectivity while reviewing a published paper?

options.A: Authors will sue the hospital if the review is too negative
options.B: Objective reviews take less time to complete than subjective ones
options.C: Journal editors require all reviews to be completely positive
options.D: Personal biases can distort the evaluation of scientific merit

explanation: Objectivity ensures that valid findings are not dismissed due to prejudice against the authors or topic. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is a primary focus when evaluating a quantitative research study?

options.B: Emotional depth of the participant interviews
options.C: Number of historical photos included in the text
options.D: Poetic imagery used in the abstract section

explanation: Quantitative research relies heavily on numerical data, statistics, and controlled measurements. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which criterion is most appropriate for judging a qualitative study instead of a quantitative one?

options.A: Data saturation and credibility of the lived experience
options.B: Strict control of confounding demographic variables
options.C: P-values calculated from large laboratory blood tests
options.D: Random assignment of patients into double-blind groups

explanation: Qualitative research explores human experiences and focuses on depth, saturation, and trustworthiness. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: Where does a structured critique framework usually begin its evaluation?
explanation: Reviewers start at the beginning with the title and abstract to understand the study scope. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the purpose of examining the methodology section during a critique?

options.A: To see how the study was conducted and data were gathered
options.B: To read the personal opinions of the hospital director
options.C: To check if the conclusion matches the introduction
options.D: To find out how much money the research project cost

explanation: The methodology reveals the nuts and bolts of the study design, showing whether the approach was sound. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h5)

question: What does attrition bias refer to in a research study?

options.A: Dishonesty of the authors when writing the abstract
options.B: Failure of the laboratory equipment during testing
options.C: Bias caused by choosing a sample from only one ward
options.D: Loss of participants over the course of the study

explanation: Attrition bias occurs when participants drop out, potentially skewing the final results. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is overgeneralization a major weakness in published research?

options.A: It claims results apply to populations not actually tested
options.B: It makes the reference list too long for readers to check
options.C: It uses complex statistical terms that nurses cannot understand
options.D: It hides the funding source from the journal editors

explanation: Overgeneralizing stretches conclusions beyond what the sample data can safely support. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: After finding a research article to be valid and relevant, what should a nurse do next?

options.A: Collaborate with colleagues to plan clinical implementation
options.B: Publish the exact same study in a local newspaper
options.C: File the paper away and wait for a doctor to notice it
options.D: Destroy all old textbooks stored in the nursing office

explanation: Valid research must be systematically translated into practice to benefit patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why is monitoring patient outcomes necessary after introducing a researched change?

options.A: To confirm if the new practice truly improves clinical care
options.B: To prove to the hospital accountant that money was spent well
options.C: To satisfy legal requirements for nursing license renewal
options.D: To ensure the original authors get cited in future audits

explanation: Tracking outcomes ensures that the new evidence actually delivers the expected benefits in real-world practice. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h7)
